subject: CipherPay: Stabilization summit & customer status — throughput/error spike
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@cipherpay.io>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@cipherpay.io
Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Production spike: error rate + throughput regression (CipherPay)

Hi Dev,

We started seeing a large regression around 08:45 PST across our payments path. Symptoms:
- Error rate for /v1/annotate -> ~9% (normally <0.3%)
- Median throughput down ~40% (p95 queueing up)
- A lot of 500s with "kv-cache-miss" and "model execution timeout" in the logs

This is affecting live transactions — several merchants are reporting timeouts and retries. I've attached a small snippet of the logs we pulled (throughput_log_snippet.csv). Please advise immediate mitigation steps and ETA for recovery. We need an owner for this.

Thanks,
Asha Rao
SRE Lead, CipherPay
asha@cipherpay.io

Thanks Asha — apologies for the impact. I'm escalating internally and setting up a rapid stabilization summit at 09:40 PST. Short plan (triage-first):
1) Engineering (David) will pull node-level telemetry + cache eviction stats — immediate hypothesis is KV-cache churn.
2) Ops (I'll coordinate) will add a small burst of reserved inference capacity and temporarily pin traffic to the most-stable model variant.
3) CS (Marissa/Laura) will prepare a brief customer-facing note with current status and ETA.
4) If recovery not within 45m, we will commit a remediation timeline and outline credits.

We're on it. Please stay on this thread and share any additional logs or timestamps (Asha, thank you for the CSV).

—Dev

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 09:55:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: error rate + throughput regression (CipherPay)

Preliminary triage update — evidence points to sudden request-pattern skew that caused aggressive KV cache eviction on a subset of inference nodes. Details:
- Root signal: a 3x increase in short-lived session patterns starting 08:44 PST; cache TTL tuned for longer sessions, eviction thrash observed
- Observed degraded tail latency on nodes running model v2.1-optimized where kernel scheduling delayed pacing
- A subset of requests spilled to fallback path producing more 500s ("kv-cache-miss" followed by timed eviction)

Immediate actions (in-flight):
- Increasing cache TTL from 15s -> 60s on affected node pool (rolling change).
- Redirecting 20% of traffic to a more conservative variant (v2.1-stable) to reduce kernel contention.
- Spinning up two reserved workers in us-west for headroom.

Expected outcome: TTL change + scale should reduce misses in ~7–12 minutes after roll starts. I'll post node telemetry and a short PNG summary shortly.

—David
David Kim
Sr Engineering Manager, Runtime
david.kim@redwood.ai

1) Can you confirm an explicit ETA (wall-clock) when error rate is expected to be back to normal?

We have an internal incident threshold set at 11:00 PST; if we haven't seen sustained improvement by then we'll escalate internally and may pause traffic. Also please include a brief on any customer credits you intend to offer — our procurement team will want that written.

Asha

Subject: RE: Production spike: error rate + throughput regression (CipherPay) — final readout and next steps

Asha / Team — final readout and commitments from Redwood: 

Outcome summary:
- Incident window: 08:45 — 10:35 PST (full recovery confirmed at 10:35). Error rate returned to baseline (<0.5%) and throughput back within 95% of normal by 10:50 after traffic smoothing and cache TTL roll.
- Root cause: cache-eviction thrash triggered by an unexpected short-lived session spike; engineering chain fixed TTL policy and added short-term capacity.

Immediate remedial actions completed:
- Increased cache TTL on affected pool (rolled 9:58–10:05).
- Redirected traffic to v2.1-stable and spun two reserved workers in us-west for headroom.
- Post-change telemetry confirmed drop in kv-cache-miss and p95 latency.

Customer-facing items and commitments:
- We issued a one-time service credit of 20% for the impacted billing period (applied to the invoice following December) — documented in HubSpot case CPH-8921.
- We will provide a post-incident report (attached: cipherpay-requested-timeline.pdf) and schedule a technical deep-dive with the CipherPay SRE/CTO next week (Marissa to propose times).
- Short-term config: engineering to add adaptive TTL heuristics to better tolerate short-session surges. Roadmap item tracked in PROD-1104.

Action items (owners):
- David: Finalize adaptive TTL spec + rollout timeline by 2025-12-05.
- Dev: Keep CipherPay and SRE channel updated; coordinate follow-up deep-dive.
- Laura/Marissa: Confirm credit applied and sync procurement comms.

Appreciate the patience — we'll follow up with the deep-dive deck and the ticket links.

—Marissa Cole
VP Customer Success, Redwood Inference
